The feed bill goes up. The topline keeps dropping. And everyone blames the hay.

Here's what gets missed: if your horse's spine is restricted in the mid-back, he literally cannot engage the muscles that build and hold that topline. He hollows. He braces. He compensates. You add more calories and nothing changes.

Dr. Leo works with DFW horses every week who've had their nutrition dialed in for months — right feed, right protein, right work schedule — but the topline won't come. Once the spine starts moving freely, the muscles follow.

If your horse looks right from a distance but drops out behind the saddle, that's worth a conversation.
